title: Dispatch: Expose revocation position through the campaign-rule domain and read APIs (PR #524 review 5, head 459887b)
description:
External review #5118796759 (2026-09-04) of PR #524 head 459887b, semantic-system profile: CHANGES REQUIRED, ONE blocking finding. The review-4 equality-boundary fix (rev10) is CONFIRMED FIXED; everything else re-checked stands. Supervisor confirmed the new finding against the code at 459887b.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev11 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev11, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 459887b. npm ci already run.

# =============================================================
FINDING (BLOCKING) — revocation timing is persisted but erased by the .1 domain shape and the .2 read APIs.

eshyra-jhpt.2 requires persistence of the REVOCATION POSITION and read/list APIs; .5 must display supersession/revocation history through the .1/.2 APIs; ADR 0020 requires history to be attributable and replayable through the typed contract. Today:
- campaign_rule.revoked_position is durable; revokeCampaignRule writes the canonical (rev10 __future__-anchored) position; activeRows reads the RAW column; checkpoint round-trips the raw row.
- But CampaignRule (campaignRules.ts:60) has status + supersededBy and NO revokedPosition; CampaignRuleProjection (line 76) has none either; rowToRule (campaignRuleStore.ts ~226) receives row.revoked_position and drops it.
- So getCampaignRule, listCampaignRules and the value returned by revokeCampaignRule expose only status:'revoked', never WHEN. The existing tests prove the gap: they reach for raw `SELECT revoked_position FROM campaign_rule` to check it.
- Worse after rev10: the stored anchor deliberately differs from the caller's input (__future__ replaces fabricated ids), and the caller has no typed way to learn what was persisted. The supersession side is symmetric and fine (supersededBy + successor.effectivePosition); revocation is the asymmetric missing datum. Domain validation also cannot express status/revoked-position consistency because the field does not exist.

# =============================================================
REQUIRED SHAPE (supervisor decision — implement exactly this)
1. Add `readonly revokedPosition: CampaignPosition | null` to CampaignRule, directly mirroring supersededBy (required field, null when not revoked). Add `readonly revokedPosition: string | null` (formatCampaignPosition output) to CampaignRuleProjection and populate it in projectCampaignRule.
2. rowToRule hydrates it from row.revoked_position. A row with status 'revoked' and NULL revoked_position must FAIL hydration with a CampaignRuleError naming the rule (reuse/relocate the message existingIntervalEnd already uses: "revoked campaign rule 'x' is missing revoked_position"); a non-revoked row with a non-null revoked_position must also fail hydration ("only a revoked rule may carry revokedPosition" or similar). Then make activeRows and existingIntervalEnd consume rule.revokedPosition instead of re-reading the raw column, so there is ONE hydration path.
3. validateCampaignRule: `status === 'revoked'` requires non-null revokedPosition ("revoked rule must carry revokedPosition"); any other status requires null ("only a revoked rule may carry revokedPosition"). Do NOT add an ordering constraint between revokedPosition and effectivePosition — a cancelled scheduled rule legitimately stores revokedPosition < effectivePosition (rev10, E5) and is never active.
4. writeRule / the INSERT: creation already requires status 'active', so the inserted revoked_position is rule.revokedPosition (null). revokeCampaignRule returns exactly what was persisted (round-5 property) — it already re-reads via getCampaignRule, so once rowToRule hydrates, the returned object carries the canonical position.
5. Export nothing new from the root index unless already exported there; CampaignRule is already on /internal.
6. Update every CampaignRule literal in src and tests (`supersededBy: null` sites: campaignRules.test.ts, contextAssembler.test.ts, campaignRuleStore.test.ts, orchestrator.test.ts, discovery/discoveryStages.test.ts, checkpoint.restore.test.ts, discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts) to add `revokedPosition: null`. Replace the tests' raw `SELECT revoked_position` assertions with typed getCampaignRule/listCampaignRules assertions (keep at most ONE raw-SQL assertion if it is proving the column itself, and say why).
7. Discovery/oracle projection fixtures that compare projections (toEqual) must include the new projection field; check the discovery probes and oracle seam still agree on both sides.

Do NOT change: migrations (the CHECK `status='revoked' => revoked_position IS NOT NULL` stays as is), the position encoding, activeRows semantics, rev10 admission, eshyra-jhpt.2.5 / eshyra-umyb / eshyra-l30k, or any round 1-6 property.

# =============================================================
PERMANENT EVIDENCE (reviewer's list — typed-API boundary, each must FAIL against 459887b)
R1. A prospective revocation's return value carries the exact canonical stored revokedPosition; getCampaignRule and listCampaignRules return the same position afterward.
R2. The rev10 future-anchor case: caller supplies fabricated session/turn ids at ordinal current+1 (and the 999999 case); the returned/read revokedPosition is the canonical {__future__, __future__, ordinal}, not the caller's anchor.
R3. Active and superseded records read back with revokedPosition null; a revoked row without revoked_position cannot hydrate (insert such a row bypassing the CHECK — e.g. via a raw INSERT with the constraint satisfied then an UPDATE, or by constructing the row in a test double — and assert the hydration error message); validateCampaignRule rejects status/revokedPosition mismatches in both directions with the distinctive messages.
R4. Checkpoint restore followed by getCampaignRule/listCampaignRules reproduces the same revokedPosition (extend checkpoint.restore.test.ts, which already captures campaign rules).
R5. A management-history style assertion obtains effective, supersession (supersededBy + successor effective) and revocation timing for a chain (create -> supersede -> revoke successor) using ONLY .2 APIs, no SQL.
Every negative assertion asserts the distinctive guard message. NEGATIVE PROOF: run the new/changed tests against 459887b before fixing and report observed failed/passed counts (type errors from the new required field count as failures — report them as such).

VERIFICATION
npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution.
